SEC Announces Agenda for Investor Advisory Committee Meeting

Published 2026-10-06 02:30 UTC

The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced the agenda for the next meeting of its Investor Advisory Committee, which will be held at the SEC's headquarters in Washington, D.C., and webcast live on the SEC's website.

The meeting will open with remarks from the Chair and commissioners, followed by a panel discussion on retail investor access to private markets. Panelists will discuss proposals to expand the definition of accredited investor, the growth of interval funds and other vehicles that offer exposure to private companies, and the risks of illiquidity and limited disclosure.

A second panel will examine the use of artificial intelligence by broker-dealers and investment advisers in communicating with retail investors. Panelists will consider how firms disclose the use of these tools, how conflicts of interest are managed, and how investors can understand recommendations generated with the help of predictive analytics.

The committee will also hear an update from its subcommittee on market structure regarding payment for order flow and best execution. The subcommittee is expected to present draft recommendations for discussion, which the full committee may vote on at a future meeting.

The Investor Advisory Committee was established by the Dodd-Frank Act to advise the Commission on regulatory priorities and initiatives that affect investors. Its members include representatives of individual investors, institutional investors, state securities regulators and investor advocates.

Members of the public may submit written comments for the committee's consideration through the SEC's website. The meeting is open to the public, and seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

The agenda, a list of panelists and instructions for accessing the webcast are posted on the committee's page on the SEC's website. An archived video of the meeting and a transcript will be available following the meeting. Questions about the meeting may be directed to the committee's staff.
